god_package.question: Does this directory contain a focused, manageable set of modules rather than acting as a 'god package' with dozens of unrelated files?

junk_drawer_module.question: Does this directory have a specific, well-defined domain responsibility rather than acting as a catch-all junk-drawer package (such as 'utils', 'helpers', 'misc', or 'common')?

flat_structure.question: Are files organized into subpackages when appropriate rather than dumping an excessive number of files into one flat directory?

excessive_nesting_depth.question: Is the directory nesting depth shallow and reasonable (e.g. 3 levels or fewer) rather than excessively deep?

inconsistent_naming_convention.question: Do all file names and subdirectory names in this directory follow a consistent naming convention (such as snake_case) rather than mixing different naming styles?

trivial_subpackage.question: Does this package contain a meaningful set of files rather than being a trivial subpackage with only one or two files?

test_structure_mismatch.question: Do test directories mirror the package layout of the source code they cover rather than using a mismatched or disorganized test structure?

barrel_file_sprawl.question: Are package exports kept minimal and purposeful rather than sprawling excessive barrel or index files that only re-export symbols across every subpackage?

circular_package_dependencies.question: Do packages and subpackages in this directory tree maintain a clean, acyclic dependency flow rather than importing from each other in circular dependencies?

layering_violation.question: Do imports in this directory flow inward toward core domain abstractions (e.g. cli/entrypoints -> infrastructure -> core/domain) rather than inner layers importing from outer layers?

god_file_or_class.question: Are all files in this directory reasonably sized (e.g. under 300 lines) rather than overly large 'god' files or classes?

duplicate_modules.question: Are the files in this directory distinct in purpose rather than near-duplicate modules with redundant classes/functions?

leaky_abstraction.question: Are third-party frameworks, HTTP clients, and ML/ORM libraries confined to outer infrastructure or entrypoint layers rather than leaking into core domain models?

business_logic_in_presentation_layer.question: Do CLI, UI, and route-handler modules delegate business logic to application services rather than implementing core domain logic directly in the presentation layer?

dead_code_module.question: Are the modules in this directory actively imported and used by other modules in the project rather than sitting as dead, unreferenced code?

missing_package_public_api.question: Does this package expose a clean public interface (such as via __init__.py exports for multi-file internal modules) rather than requiring callers to import deep internal implementation files directly?

scattered_feature_logic.question: Are the files within this directory cohesive and focused on a single architectural concern rather than scattering feature logic across unrelated modules?

inconsistent_architectural_style.question: Does the structure of this directory follow a clean layered/hexagonal architecture consistent with its subpackages rather than mixing conflicting architectural patterns?
